DELETE-THE-FIX, CONFIRMED: built a control-clone (node tools/control-clone.mjs, writable=game/src/render/actor.js) and reverted the four identifiers back to the colliding names IN THE CLONE ONLY. First attempt gave a false all-green because tools/visual/w1-f1-critic-shader-collision.mjs hardcodes entry:'game/index.html' internally and SILENTLY IGNORES a --entry CLI flag (path.resolve()s the literal against process.cwd(), never against args.entry) — a real bug in that tool, worth fixing separately, that I worked around by cd-ing into the clone before invoking node so process.cwd() resolved correctly. That corrected run reproduced the ORIGINAL failure byte-for-byte in shape: 124 duplicate declarations, 66/124 FAILED TO LINK, identical GLSL errors. Saved to artifacts/.../delete-the-fix/. CENSUS TRIPWIRE, WRITTEN, RUN, AND PROVEN (follow-up 1, the one the verdict called the important half): added a NO-UNRUNNABLE-PROGRAM-IN-SCENE check to tools/visual/w1-30-surface-orphan-census.mjs that reads program.diagnostics.runnable off the renderer's live WebGLProperties for every material actually mounted in the scene. Ran it two ways: (a) PLAIN, against current fixed HEAD — 0 findings, all 5 pre-existing checks still PASS. (b) RED-ARM, against a second control-clone with the collision reintroduced the same way as the delete-the-fix arm — the new check alone went FAIL with 66 materials flagged and the exact original GLSL errors, while the other 5 checks correctly STAYED GREEN (they measure hook installation, which is genuinely unaffected — proving the new check catches a class the other 5 structurally cannot, which is the whole point). This satisfies RULES rule 4 (breaking the thing on purpose to see the probe go red) for the new check specifically. Discovered and fixed an inaccurate comment while doing this: three.js only populates a program's `.diagnostics` when there is a LINK FAILURE to report — a successfully-linked program leaves it `undefined` forever, not just 'before its first compile' as I'd first assumed and written. Fixed the comment and the check's PASS-detail text to say this accurately rather than the wrong 'not yet compiled' framing; the check's actual PASS/FAIL logic was already correct throughout (only a positive runnable:false ever counts as a finding) so this was a documentation fix, not a logic fix.
